text.p: Steelworkers Tuesday approved a new five-year contract with Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel Corp., ending a strike that began Oct. 1, the United Steelworkers of America said.
Union members voted by 3,105 to 817 to approve the contract.
"This contract represents a great victory for organised labour," said Jim Bowen, chairman of the United Steelworkers negotiating committee.
The contract, which is effective immediately and expires Sept. 1, 2002, covers 4,500 USWA members at eight Wheeling-Pittsburgh facilities in Pennsylvania, Ohio and West Virginia.

The contract includes a $2 million fund to reimburse workers for medical expenses incurred during the strike; a $2,000 signing bonus; $1.50 an hour in wage increases, and weekly payments of $200 plus health insurance pending a return to work, the union said.

Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel Chief Executive Officer John Scheessele called the vote a "strong indication that our workers believe they have a fair contract and are ready to return to the business of making quality steel for our customers."
Scheessele said the company would immediately begin the process of recalling workers, but cautioned that it would be a gradual process.
"We will bring people back as quickly as we can, based on the level of orders for steel that we receive," Scheessele said.
